# Pixel Studio Edit

> Pixel Studio Edit is a free, open-source pixel art and text editor that runs
> entirely in your browser. Text graphics, photo editing and pixel art share one
> canvas, one set of editable layers and one export. There is no account, no
> install and no upload: the image you open stays on your machine.

The site is a single static page — `index.html` plus plain JavaScript modules,
self-hosted web fonts and a service worker. It is MIT licensed and deployable to
any static host.

## What it is for

- Making a banner, poster, story, meme or thumbnail from text and shapes,
  without an account or a subscription.
- Editing a photo in the browser — crop, scale, adjust, remove a background, add
  text — with the pixels never leaving the device.
- Turning a photo into pixel art: palette snapping, dithering and a pixel grid.

## Where the work happens

- Everything — drawing, layers, text styling, filters, dithering, PNG/JPEG/WebP
  export, project save and load — runs in the browser tab. Nothing is uploaded
  and no API key is involved.
- The **Nirbhar** toolkit (fourteen offline tools: background remover, photo
  enhancer, upscaler, halftone, seamless tiles, palette studio, PDF maker, icon
  and sprite-sheet pack, SVG export, generative art, ID photo sheet, collage,
  watermark, batch convert) is plain JavaScript with no dependency and no model
  download.
- One optional feature reaches the network: **AI remove background (beta)**. The
  first use fetches a segmentation model — about 40 MB, once — from
  `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and Hugging Face. The image is processed locally and is
  never uploaded. If the model cannot be loaded, the colour-based remover runs
  instead.

## Pages

- [Editor](https://galeoindus.github.io/pixelstudioedit/): the whole application
  — start screen, canvas, tool rail, panels, Nirbhar.
- [Nirbhar manual](https://github.com/galeoindus/pixelstudioedit/blob/main/docs/NIRBHAR_MANUAL.md):
  what each of the fourteen tools does and where its limits are (English and
  Hindi).
- [Source](https://github.com/galeoindus/pixelstudioedit): the repository, the
  issue tracker and the licence.

## Notes for automated readers

- This is an application, not a library of articles: there is one HTML page, and
  its content is the editor itself. The interactive panels need JavaScript.
- `sitemap.xml` lists that one page, at its canonical address
  `https://galeoindus.github.io/pixelstudioedit/`.
- `robots.txt` allows every crawler.
- The page's structured data is a `WebApplication` entry describing the editor,
  its price (free), its licence and its features.
